summary:
A player can move a whole sword any distance along X, Y and Z, turn it by any angle, and flip it across the fixed planes x = 0 and z = 0. No step re-centres it before analysis. Canonical's C1–C7 touch a position only to turn −0 into +0, the server takes designs through Canonical.draft only, and Analyze.run prepares every part from part.pos as given. Forged items render anchored to their own bounds, so on a stand or in a viewport such a move cannot be seen.

What the SPEC promises:
- Y and Z translation invariance, except three named classes: (h) a face typed exactly TIE from a probe's line, (j) sampled overlaps and the |z| rank reorder, and (k) a part flush at a slanted hidden gap.
- Mirror invariance across x = 0 and z = 0, except rank ties up to the sign, round copies that coincide on the model, and Thinness' +X walk sign.
- Ids and part order change nothing, to the bit.
- Another writing of a part changes nothing, except class (i).
- X shifts and whole-sword rotations are 'real changes': Asymmetry is measured about x = 0, the raster's columns start at x = 0, and the difficulty axis is +Y.

Both ranks key on |cx| and |cz| for one reason only: so the editor's two mirrors cannot reorder parts. When the rank took cz directly, 545 of 8,000 Z-mirrored tangles swapped which twin keeps a shared face (E-S2.12). Every sampling grid is already anchored to its own part (§4.3 rules out a global grid). The only world anchors left are the ranks' place keys, Asymmetry's plane and the raster's columns (these two along X, on purpose) and the hitbox (a validation rule only).

Three mechanisms make a shift move G; all were measured on scratch copies:
- **J1, the measure rank's |z| key.** It accounts for 1,971 of the 2,081 designs whose G moves under a Z shift.
- **J2, the flush-contact test.** MassProps.ownership pre-tests overlap with aabbOverlap(p, q, 0) at L368. For parts that are exactly flush, rounding of the world bounds decides whether a part that merely touches enters `higher`. That set sizes the sampled overlap boxes, switches between exact and sampled clipping, sets the design-wide hOverlap ladder and feeds Asymmetry's work estimate. It accounts for all 110 Z moves left after J1 and all 357 Y moves.
- **J3, the cell count.** ceil(extent/h) at L289 sits exactly on a whole number for tidy sizes. It shows only under random shifts.

A scratch fix covers all three:
- the measure rank keyed on the kept Grip parts' point, with place keys rounded to 1e-9;
- a margin of −OVERLAP_TOL at L368;
- ceil(extent/h − 1e-9) at L289.

With it, every Parity fixture and Gen design analyses bit for bit as before except C04: its M2 volume moves by −1e-6 and G is unchanged at 4 decimals. No G, M2 volume or kept set moves on the plausible third shifted 0.037 down Z or 0.3317 along Y, nor on 494 designs × 4 random Y/Z shifts. The committed tree moves G on 2,081, 357 and 158 of them. Mirror images and id shuffles read exactly as on the committed tree, and the cost change is within noise under load.

Candidate (a), normalising position, closes neither J2 nor J3, and any reference taken before the verdict can be moved by hidden parts. Candidate (c), anchoring grids to the design, has nothing to re-anchor. The repo was not changed. findings: Q1 Moves. 'Transforms are free: snapping is a tool the player sets per transform type, never a storage grid' (SPEC §11 L2847-2849). The Move tool sets each selected part to p_i + snap(Δ)·A (§11.6 L2975). Ctrl+A selects every visible part (L2966). With several parts selected, 'Position = pivot (moves the group)' and 'Rotate by' turns it (§11.9 L3044-3045). Arrows and PageUp/PageDown nudge by the Move step (§11.6 L2994-2996). Move snapping is on at 0.05 by default, Shift inverts it, and free values are never touched (§11.8 L3021, L3028-3033). So a whole sword can be moved along X, Y and Z by any amount.

Q1 Rotation. The Rotate tool applies 'q_i' = q(N, θ) ⊗ q_i, p_i' = c + R(N, θ)·(p_i − c) (the same angle for every part and for its centre)' about c, 'centre of the selection's exact extents' (§11.6 L2976, L2991-2992). Rotate snapping is off by default (§11.8 L3022), and Ctrl+R/Ctrl+T turn by 90° (L2993-2995). So a whole sword can be turned by any angle about blueprint, local or view axes.

Q1 Mirror. M copies across x = 0 and Shift+M across z = 0. 'Flip in place' replaces each selected part by Mirror.reflect(part, plane) (§11.10 L3071-3075). The planes are fixed (§3.8 L711-713; src/shared/Blueprint/Mirror.luau L1-5). 'C Centre on axis moves the selection so the centre of its extents is on x = 0' (§11.10 L3075-3076; §3.8 L735-736).

Q1 Bounds. Every move and rotate path clamps |pos_k| ≤ 16 (§11.7 L3006-3007; Limits.luau L9; C2 in §3.5 L646). 'The hitbox is not a constraint (overflow is shown)' (§11.7 L3013), but V2 OutOfHitbox is an error: the world AABB must lie within the hitbox ± EPS_CONTAIN (§4.2 L858; Analyze.luau L161-170), and 'errors block Forge' (§11.12 L3105). The hitbox runs from (−0.8, 0, −0.3) to (0.8, 5, 0.3), with 'Origin = centre of the hitbox's bottom face', centred on x = 0 and z = 0 (§3.1 L514-517, L522-524; EquipmentTypes.luau L5, L32-33). So a forgeable whole-design move is any (dx, dy, dz) within the hitbox's slack. Moved 0.037 down Z, 246 of 11,129 plausible designs leave the hitbox.

Q1 No normalisation anywhere.
- Canonical's C1–C7 change a position only by C5, −0 → +0 (§3.5 L645-651; Canonical.luau L8-19, L108-109).
- 'No storage grid: positions, sizes and quaternions stay the doubles the editor produced, so the stored, analysed and rendered design is exactly what the player built' (§3.5 L640-641).
- The server takes client data through Canonical.draft, 'the only entry point for client blueprint data' (§3.6 L670).
- Pipeline.analyze asserts the core is canonical, then calls Analyze.run (§4.8 L1206-1207).
- Analyze.run prepares every part from part.pos as given (Analyze.luau L131-142; Shapes.luau L118-119: cx, cy, cz = part.pos).
- WorkSet.select only picks indices (WorkSet.luau L15-37).

Q1 Visibility. Stands render with anchor BaseCenter; workpieces and viewports render Center (§13.7 L3541, L3550; RenderPlan.luau L16-18, L160-167). Both are anchored to the design's own bounds, so a whole-design move is invisible on a forged item. The editor stage places parts relative to the fixed hitbox centre HC. It draws the hitbox ghost and the centre plane x = 0, plus a grid on z = 0 (and the z = 0 plane while Shift+M is used) (§11.2 L2883-2887, L2896-2900; §3.1 L516-517). There a move shows only against those references.

Q1 Frames.
- gripPoint is the volume-weighted centroid of the kept Grip parts, 'the origin if none is kept' (§4.5 L1069; MassProps.luau L494-519, L534-542).
- The physics axis is the XY projection of the parts' votes (§4.5 L1070).
- V4 uses every Grip part (§4.2 L860; MassProps.luau L522-530).
- 'Difficulty frame = point of the kept Grip parts, axis fixed at blueprint +Y (Thinness length, edge facing test, the trace's frame), consistent with the fixed plane x = 0: no grip part, visible or hidden, can steer a factor' (§4.5 L1081-1083; MassProps.luau L27-28, L545-554).
These points move with the design. The axes are world directions, so turning the design is a real change.

Q2 Y and Z translation promised.
- 'a Y shift moves neither Thinness nor the edge' (§5 promise L1312-1313).
- 'The raster's cells are therefore Y and Z translation-exact, and so is their thickness but where a part lies flush with the face a line leaves for a slanted hidden gap' (§4.6 L1092-1095).
- Douglas–Peucker runs on the integer lattice, 'so a Y shift ... keeps every chain and length to the bit' (§4.6 L1134-1136).
- §5.6 has a Y/Z translation row (L1549).
- T-DIF-07 (a) (§14.6 L3840-3846): F and C fixtures moved by E-S2.10's offsets (Invariance.spec L83-85: Y 0.013, 0.125 and 0.3317; Z 0.01 and −0.037; and (0.2, 0.05)). Bounds: |Δx_f| ≤ TOL_FACTOR_ABS 0.02 and |ΔG| ≤ TOL_G_INVARIANT 0.002 (Tol.luau L21-22). Along Y, G and EdgeLength must hold to the bit.
Named exceptions:
- (h) a face typed exactly TIE from a probe's line (§5.2 L1436-1438);
- (j) M2's sampled overlaps and the measure rank's |z| reorder (§4.4 L944-946; §5 L1327-1332; §17.1 O11 (j), L4738);
- (k) a part flush with the face a line leaves for a slanted hidden gap (§4.6 L1093-1095; O11 (k)).

Q2 Not promised: X and rotation.
- 'X shifts and whole-sword rotations are real changes' (§14.6 L3855).
- Gen.translated: 'X never moves (an X shift is a real change to Asymmetry, SPEC §14.6 T-DIF-07)' (tests/lib/Gen.luau L876-877).
- Asymmetry is 'left/right about the fixed plane x = 0' (§5.2 L1442-1449; Factors.luau L65, L611, L657-658).
- The raster's x is 'anchored at the plane x = 0 (mirror-symmetric cells)' (§4.6 L1087-1088; Edge.luau L19-22, L361-363, L419-420).
- C15 is 'rotated 4° about Z (a real change against the fixed frame)' (§5.5 L1529).
- A27 shifts F1's hilt 0.04 in X: Hammering 0.1037 → 0.1537, 'a visible asymmetry' (SPEC-evidence E-S2.7 L248).

Q2 Mirror across x = 0 and z = 0 promised, with exceptions.
- 'a mirror image across X or Z reads its original's, but for parts that tie in the rank up to the sign of x or z (true twins among them), round copies that coincide on the model and Thinness' walk, which signs a local axis along X up the world, +X ... (a generated design's whole X mirror image: ΔD up to 0.0621 over 150, no flip; E-S2.13)' (§5.6 L1541; the same exceptions in §17.2 L4751).
- 'A mirror image's cells are its mirror' (§4.6 L1095-1096).
- 'A design mirrored with Blueprint/Mirror measures 0' for Asymmetry (§5.2 L1453; T-DIF-08 §14.6 L3857-3860), and 'A tool-mirrored design measures exactly symmetric' (§11.10 L3075).
- Round models stand in world frames, so 'the model of a mirror image (§3.8) is the mirror of the model' (§4.4 L959-962).
- Thickness (Z) asymmetry is not measured (§5.2 L1454).

Q2 Ids, order and writings.
- 'so that invisible choices of id and order cannot move a tier (§5)' (§4.4 L929-930).
- 'Every factor walks W in the measure's rank order ..., so no id and no part order reaches a factor (T-DIF-07)' (§5.2 L1402).
- 'any order of a design's parts gives the same verdicts, readings, units, areas and contact rows to the bit' (§17.2 L4751).
- T-DIF-07 (c) (§14.6 L3850-3851) and T-PHY-09 (L3806-3809) test this.
- θ and a polyhedron's walk are the solid's (§5.2 L1403-1409; T-DIF-07 (d) L3852-3855). The exception is M2's surface samples of a round part, a Wedge, or a Block straddling another part's hiding boundary, which follow the writing (§5.2 L1404-1407; O11 (i)).
- Hidden filler and specks cannot move a tier (§5 L1293-1294), and dust is held to the bit (T-DIF-04/05, §14.6 L3818-3823; A14 is F1 with 19 attached dust cubes, Adversarial.luau L529-557).

Q3 The rank keys in code.
- The verdict's key is { -v, cy, |cx|, cx, |cz|, cz, h1, h2, h3 }, with the slot name compared after the volume (Sampling.luau L505, L513-515).
- The measure's key is { -volume, cy, |cx|, cx, |cz|, cz, hx, hy, hz, ux..vz }, then slot, material and index (L551-552, L561-567).
- The reason is in the comment at L482-483: '|cx| before cx, |cz| before cz: a mirror image across either centre plane can only swap parts that tie on all of it'.
- cy is used raw. A Y shift keeps the order, and the fixer's rankcmp found no reorder along Y.

Q3 Why |cx| and |cz| (history).
- E-S2.12 (SPEC-evidence L640-643): '8,000 X / Z mirror images of tangles: 548 verdicts differ, 545 of them near twins stacked in z that swap which keeps a coincident face, because the rank took cz directly, and 3 exact ties; the build ranks |cz| before cz, as |x| before x (§4.4)'. L646-650: with |cz|, the measure differs from the earlier rank on 20 designs, each one where the key changes the order.
- E-S2.5 X01 (L225): two blade copies at z ±0.003 give ΔD 0.0002 with |z| before z, and 0.0010 under the rank before it.
- .build-notes\m2x\m2x_fixer_r2.json: the verdict rank's place keys (cy, |cx|, cx, |cz|, cz) were written in M2x fix round 2. .build-notes\m2x_journal_r2.txt L6: 'Sampling.ranked puts |cz| before cz'.
- m2x_v2_r3 to r6: the 26 plausible and 10 corpus quiet measure moves are 'all from the |cz| key'.
So the absolute-value keys serve the editor's two mirror planes only, and |cz| is the only Z-anchored element of the analysis.

Q3 Mechanism J2 (measured), the flush-contact test.
- MassProps.ownership builds `higher` with 'if aabbOverlap(p, q, 0) then ... if (Gjk.within(p, q, OVERLAP_TOL))' (MassProps.luau L368-370).
- L78 says 'OVERLAP_TOL = 1e-9 -- parts that merely touch own their whole volume; GJK decides at this gap'. §16.18 (L4513) lists OVERLAP_TOL among guards that 'separate rounding from geometry'.
- For exactly flush parts, the margin-0 box test decides instead of GJK, and the rounding of the world bounds decides the box test (Shapes.luau L157-185).
- `higher` sizes the sampled overlap boxes (L262-282), switches between exact and sampled clipping (L390), sets the design-wide ladder hOverlap (L402-421) and enters Asymmetry's work estimate (Factors.luau L637: (1 + #mirrors + #aboves)).

Q3 Mechanism J3 (measured), the cell count. cellsPerAxis takes ceil(extent / h) (MassProps.luau L284-290), with the extent taken from world bounds through toLocal. For tidy sizes the ratio is exactly a whole number, and the rounding of a shifted design can add a row of cells.

Q4 Constraints for a fix.
- §4.1 L829-836: only + − × ÷ and sqrt, floor, ceil, abs, min, max; numeric loops; sorts with total orders; no module state.
- S-PAR-02 digests Dump.canonical(Analyze.run(core, {measureInvalid = true})) for every Parity fixture and Tol.PARITY_DESIGNS Gen designs (S-PAR-02.luau L15-20; Parity.spec L45-47; §14.10 L3986-3988). It requires Analyze, Canonical, Balance, EquipmentTypes, Limits and Materials (S-PAR-02.luau L120-130), so all of Physics is in it.
- S-PAR-01 requires Canonical, ItemModelBuilder, Limits, Quat, RenderPlan, Shapes and World (S-PAR-01.luau L124-133) and calls Shapes.prepare, toWorld and sd (L272-273, L333, L418). It loads none of Sampling, MassProps, Analyze, Edge or Factors.
- Goldens: 'Changed outcome code shows as a golden diff, which also needs a bump. Workflow: edit → bump BALANCE_VERSION → --bless → review → commit' (§14.9 L3948-3956). The digest's file name carries BALANCE_VERSION (Parity.spec L38-39).
- Outputs stay in blueprint space: com and gripPoint (§4.7 L1162-1166), blueprint-XY chains (L1168), the edge's gripPoint (L1169-1170), the editor overlays (§11.13 L3137). PrecisionTrace maps the edge as (p − g)·A (§6.10 L1777).
- The blueprint format is in §3.3 L572-582.

candidates:
(a) Normalise position before analysis.
What it needs:
- A reference taken before the verdict, because the verdict runs on the normalised parts.
- Z only. X must stay in the world frame: Asymmetry is about x = 0 (§5.2 L1442), the raster's columns start at x = 0 (§4.6 L1088), and X shifts are real changes (§14.6 L3855). Y needs nothing: the rank's raw cy keeps its order under a Y shift, and the raster's rows start at Y0. Normalising Y would also change every fixture's inputs, since none has its lowest point at 0.
- Shifted copies of PartData made after V1–V2 (inputs stay unchanged, §14.5 L3786).
- com, gripPoint and edge.gripPoint put back into blueprint space, which costs rounding.
What it closes: J1, provided the place keys are still rounded. Twins symmetric about the reference otherwise tie only up to rounding.
What it does not close: J2 and J3. The normalised coordinates of a shifted copy differ in their last bits (fl(fl(cz + t) − fl(r + t)) ≠ cz − r), and those flips are decided at the last bit.
Risks:
- Hidden parts can move every pre-verdict reference: A14's dust cubes put every Grip part's point at z 0.00168 (measured), a speck at the box's edge moves the box, and an Enclosed sliver can poke out. Every coordinate then shifts with the hidden part, which breaks 'dust held to the bit' (T-DIF-04/05) by construction.
- Fixtures whose reference is not 0 change their inputs: 32 of 136 for the box's z, 33 for every Grip part's point. Their goldens and the S-PAR-02 digest move, which needs a BALANCE_VERSION bump.
What it keeps: S-PAR-01 is unaffected if Shapes is untouched.

(b) Re-key the ranks on the design's own centre.
What it needs:
- measureRanked(parts, ref) with place keys (dy, |dx|, dx, |dz|, dz) relative to the kept Grip parts' point (§4.5's physics and difficulty frame point), rounded with floor(v / 1e-9 + 0.5).
- Sampling.exposure ranks after its verdict loop, so it needs the grip slot. MassProps.ownership (L344) and Analyze L445 take the point.
- Test helpers that call these directly pass the point too: Analyze.spec L768, DifficultyHelpers L106-111 and L206, Edge.spec L121-122 and L152, Reference.spec L74, PhysicsHelpers L90-91.
What it keeps (measured):
- Every Parity fixture and Gen design is bit-identical, because no rank order changes.
- Mirror images across x = 0 and z = 0 read exactly as on the committed tree. Under §3.8's closed forms the point is the mirror of the point up to rounding, and the 1e-9 rounding absorbs that.
- Id shuffles change nothing.
- §4.1 holds: + − × ÷ and floor only, and the sort stays a strict total order with the index last.
- Hidden parts cannot move the point (kept parts only).
- The blueprint format, S-PAR-01 and the S-PAR-02 digest are untouched.
What it closes: J1 (Z list 2,081 → 110), and the X component of the rank by construction.
Risks:
- The verdict's rank (Sampling.ranked L505) runs before kept parts are known. It stays world-keyed: under the Z shift its order changed on 1,997 movers, yet re-keying it moved no G and no kept set. Or it is keyed on a pre-verdict point: the non-Dust box changed no digest line and kept mirrors and ids, but hidden parts can nudge it.
- Parts within 1e-9 of each other now tie on place, and turn, slot, material and index decide. This is the sub-1e-9 class the SPEC already concedes for TIE (§5.2 L1436-1438).

(c) Anchor the sampling grids to the design. Along Y and Z there is nothing to re-anchor:
- every grid is already part-anchored (§4.3 L881-882, E-S2.4);
- the X anchors (Asymmetry's plane, the raster's columns) are deliberate.
